data.name: Orion
data.gender_notes: Orion is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Orion was a giant hunter who boasted that he could kill any animal in the world. Gaia, the Earth goddess, in revenge sent a scorpion to kill him. Orion's body was placed among the stars, forming the constellation of the same name. The name Orion carries the meaning “Hunter in the heavens” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Orion usually hope their child will grow to embody hunter in the heavens and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of determination, courage, and strength in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Orion belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hunter in the heavens.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Orion total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: אוריון
in_hebrew.meaning: אוריון - השם מתייחס לכוכב או לשומר השמיים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אוריון הוא שם שמקורו בשמי העברית ומתייחס לכוכב או לשומר השמיים. הוא אחד משמות הכוכבים המוכרים ביותר בתרבויות שונות, כולל היהדות והנצרות. השם אוריון קשור לכוכב הציד הגדול שמופיע בשמי הלילה ומסמל את האור וההדרכה.

in_greek.name: Ωρίων
in_greek.meaning: Ωρίων - το όνομα σχετίζεται με τον κυνηγό 별
in_greek.long_meaning: Ωρίων είναι το όνομα ενός από τους πιο φωτεινούς αστερισμούς στον ουρανό, που σχετίζεται με τον κυνηγό της ελληνικής μυθολογίας. Ο Ορίων ήταν ένας ισχυρός και γενναίος κυνηγός που τοποθετήθηκε ανάμεσα στα άστρα από τον θεό Διόνυσο. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Ορίων, αλλά η παράδοση και η ιστορία της Εκκλησίας έχουν συνδέσει το όνομα με την πνευματική σημασία του κυνηγού και του οδηγού.

in_latin.name: Orion
in_latin.meaning: Orion - the name refers to the constellation or the hunter
in_latin.long_meaning: Orion, a name derived from ancient Greek mythology, refers to the constellation named after the hunter Orion. In Christian tradition, the name symbolizes guidance, strength, and the pursuit of spiritual truth. The early Christian church recognized the constellation as a symbol of the light of Christ guiding humanity through the darkness.

in_english.name: Orion
in_english.meaning: Orion - a constellation name symbolizing guidance and strength
in_english.long_meaning: The name Orion originates from ancient Greek mythology, referring to a mighty hunter placed among the stars. In Christian tradition, Orion symbolizes the light of Christ and spiritual guidance. The name is associated with qualities such as courage, strength, and leadership. Historically, the constellation Orion has been a significant navigational aid and a symbol of hope in many cultures, including Christianity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Orion has been passed down through centuries due to its association with the constellation and Greek mythology. It is often used as a name for ships, telescopes, and even towns in various parts of the world. The constellation of Orion is also a popular motif in art and literature, representing strength, fearlessness, and the vastness of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the constellation of Orion can be seen as a symbol of perseverance and faith in the face of challenges. Orion's boast of being able to kill any animal can be interpreted as the human tendency to overestimate our abilities and assume control over our lives. However, the inevitable arrival of the scorpion serves as a reminder of the importance of humility and surrender to a higher power. Thus, the name Orion can inspire us to trust in God and face our fears with faith and courage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Orion represents the watchful protector in the night sky, guiding Christians through the spiritual darkness and leading them toward the celestial light of God. In the constellation's pattern, Christians may find reflection of their faith journey, with its unwavering commitment and steadfastness.

biblical_reference.note: Although Orion is not directly mentioned in the Bible, it is referenced in Job 38:31, Amos 5:8, and Isaiah 13:10, relating to its celestial significance.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Orion was a Greek mythological hunter and a constellation in the night sky. The name Orion carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
